$comment: Gate B DRAFT rule object for RF-SEV-005 — pending, NON-EXECUTABLE. Authored only from RF Clinical Rule Specification v1.2 §9.6 and the RF-SEV-005 inventory entry. Mixed-source rule. Expresses reported fibrosis/scar PROVENANCE-TAGGED HISTORY structure only: a user-reported phrase (fibrosis, scar, lump, tightness, different sensation, old injury site) is stored in injury_history_modifier with provenance and confirmation status, structural uncertainty preserved, and is NOT placed in the current structural profile unless a valid report supports it. Self-report alone has no independent effect on identity, severity, prognosis, progression, monitoring threshold, or readiness. QRF-045 applies only as reference context to the separate chronic structural pathway. No diagnosis, recurrence-risk, progression, rehab, dosage, exercise-selection, confidence, phase, plan, or return-to-sport logic; raw media not interpreted; defers to RF-DX-006 and RF-SAF-006; safety precedence preserved. Not approved. Not wired into any runtime.
rule_title: Reported fibrosis/scar is provenance-tagged history, not severity

input_contract.$comment: Structural reported-history inputs taken verbatim-in-meaning from v1.2 §9.6. Stored in injury_history_modifier with provenance + confirmation status; never inferred; raw media is never interpreted here.

decision_contract.$comment: Provenance-tagged history structure only. The report is stored with provenance/confirmation status and preserves structural uncertainty; it has no independent effect on identity, severity, prognosis, progression, monitoring, or readiness, and is never upgraded. No raw-media interpretation, no numeric values, no phase/rehab/plan/RTS. Safety precedence preserved.

notes: Mixed normative source; MUST; permitted_use evidence_record_only. Architecture refs preserved per source: V3.1-4 and V3.1-5 (context gate / input classification), V3.1-6 (anchor quality), V3.1-8 (separated confidence objects), V3.1-13.1 (prescription gate), V3.1-24 (confidence/evidence/output locks). Evidence grades/roles preserved per source: QRF-044 (X1) and QRF-046 (I1) limited to the prior-history / provenance role; QRF-045 (C1) applies ONLY as reference context to the separate chronic structural pathway and must not upgrade ordinary user-reported fibrosis/scar language into confirmed fibrosis, chronic structural diagnosis, prognosis, recurrence-risk, rehab, or progression logic. Per §9.6 trigger: the user reports previous fibrosis, scar, lump, tightness, or a different sensation at a prior RF site. Per §9.6 decision: store the report in injury_history_modifier, capture provenance and confirmation status, ask for available reports, and preserve structural uncertainty; do not place it in the current structural profile unless a valid report supports it. Per §9.6 no-independent-effect: self-report alone must not assign current injury identity, structural severity, prognosis, progression speed, monitoring threshold, or readiness. Per §9.6 chronic-structural separation: persistent sport-related symptoms plus valid imaging evidence of central-tendon pathology may activate a distinct external assessment/referral pathway informed only as reference context by QRF-045; this does not validate self-reported fibrosis or autonomous surgical selection. The rule clearly distinguishes user-reported vs externally reported vs imaging-confirmed fibrosis/scar vs separately-documented chronic structural pathway evidence. Reported fibrosis/scar is never inferred from symptoms, pain location, mechanism, self-tests, subjective sensation, or raw imaging; raw media is not interpreted here and requires a separately validated imaging subsystem (V3.1 §25). Report-descriptor handling defers to RF-DX-006; serious structural/restriction concerns defer to RF-SAF-006 (neither is bypassed). History-structure rule, not a safety rule, so safety_state_output is null and blocked_targets is empty; safety precedence preserved. No severity/prognosis/history model is authored here (deferred to later objects). Draft — approval_status remains pending.
